items.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools. It provides a standardized way for AI models to access external data sources, tools, and prompts through a unified protocol. The protocol defines a client-server architecture where AI assistants act as clients connecting to MCP servers that expose resources, tools, and prompts. Major companies like Anthropic, Microsoft, and others are adopting MCP as a standard for AI-tool integration. The protocol supports resources (data sources), tools (functions), and prompts (templates) through a standardized JSON-RPC protocol over various transports including stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket. Major adopters include Anthropic's Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed, and various IDE integrations. The protocol is open source and maintained by the Model Context Protocol organization on GitHub. Microsoft has announced MCP support in Azure AI Foundry and VS Code. The protocol specification is available at modelcontextprotocol.io.

Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP) is gaining traction as a standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data sources. The protocol defines a standard interface for AI models to interact with external tools, data sources, and prompts through a client-server architecture. Major IDEs like Cursor, Zed, and VS Code have added MCP support. Microsoft announced MCP support in Azure AI Foundry and VS Code. The protocol uses JSON-RPC over stdio/HTTP/WebSocket transports. Anthropic open-sourced the specification and SDKs for Python, TypeScript, and other languages. The protocol defines three core primitives: Resources (data sources), Tools (functions), and Prompts (templates). Community servers exist for databases, APIs, file systems, and more. Some criticism exists around the stdio transport limitation and the need for better authentication/authorization standards.

Model Context Protocol (MCP) - Anthropic's open standard for connecting AI assistants to external tools and data sources. The protocol defines a client-server architecture where AI assistants (clients) connect to MCP servers that expose resources, tools, and prompts. Major adoption includes Anthropic's Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed, VS Code, and Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry. The protocol uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, HTTP, and WebSocket transports. It defines three core primitives: Resources (read-only data sources), Tools (executable functions), and Prompts (reusable prompt templates). Community has built servers for PostgreSQL, GitHub, Slack, file systems, browsers, and many other services. Some criticism around stdio transport limitations, lack of standardized auth, and the need for better discovery mechanisms. Microsoft's adoption in VS Code and Azure AI Foundry signals growing enterprise adoption.

Microsoft announced MCP support in Azure AI Foundry and VS Code. Core primitives: Resources (data), Tools (functions), Prompts (templates). Community has built 100+ MCP servers for databases, APIs, file systems, browsers, and more. Some criticism around stdio transport limitations, lack of standardized authentication, and discovery mechanisms. Anthropic open-sourced the spec and SDKs. Microsoft's adoption signals enterprise readiness. Community discussions around transport improvements, auth standards, and server discovery protocols.
